                                                            Skeptics In The Pub
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 07:38:44 -0400
  Archived: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 07:38:44 -0400
  Subject: Skeptics In The Pub



  Source: Hospital Porters Against the New World Order - Blog
  http://hpanwo.blogspot.com/2008/08/skeptics-in-pub-18808.html
  18/8/08
  Skeptics In The Pub
  Ben Emlyn-Jones
  On Monday evening I went to Skeptics in the Pub:
  http://www.skeptic.org.uk/pub/
  This was the second time I've attended. Last time, last month, I
  wrote about it here:
  http://hpanwo.blogspot.com/2008/07/skeptic-in-pub-21808.html
  I arrived early at the Penderel's Oak, but was momentarily taken
  aback because it has a new signboard; it's been renamed the Left-
  Brain Arms. Clustered outside on the street were a group of
  customers huddling in self-conscious poses as they had a quick
  irrationality break (It's not been easy for them since the ban.
  The pub's landlord scoffed at my idea of setting up a separate
  irrational-thinking bar.) As before the cellar bar was
  enthusiastically crowded. The attendees looked fresh-faced and
  optimistic. These are people living the Skeptic Dream! They wear
  Skeptic clothes and eat Skeptic food; they drive Skeptic cars and
  ride on Skeptic buses! Their MBA's were pinned like figureheads
  to their chests, scintillating in the dusky wash of the overhead
  ceiling lights. I tried to order my usual tipple from the bar,
  but the barmaid curtly informed me: "I'm sorry, Sir; we're only
  serving Skeptic drinks here tonight." So I settled down with a
  cool, refreshing pint of James Randi Bitter and listened to the
  speaker.
  Doug Ellison is a multimedia designer for e-learning, but in his
  spare time is a space enthusiast. He runs a web forum dedicated
  to sharing and developing practical ideas for exploring the solar
  system:
  http://www.unmannedspaceflight.com/index.php?
  The subject of his address that evening was Mars. It's a planet
  that has come to symbolize all that is alien and unreachable, but
  in fact Mars is more similar to Earth than any other planet we've
  discovered so far. It rotates only a little bit slower so the
  Martian day is a mere 40 minutes longer. It is the only other
  place in the universe where it is known that you will find liquid
  water, albeit not much. Today it is very arid and its atmosphere
  is 100 times thinner than Earth's, but its surface shows signs
  that in the distant past it had a thicker atmosphere with a large
  amount of water: rivers, lakes and even oceans. It was once very
  Earth-like and life could have emerged there. Unfortunately
  without a strong magnetic field the water soon evaporated into
  space. With a magnetic field to protect it from solar radiation
  Mars might have been like Earth today, a blue-green planet! The


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m22-003.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:20]
Skeptics In The Pub

  question of whether life did ever occur there, or even that it
  might still be there, is one of the biggest questions in modern
  science. As a result Mars has been targeted with dozens of space
  probes from several different nations. Today there is a virtually
  permanent robotic presence there and the USA, Russia and China
  all have manned missions on their drawing boards. But Ellison
  believes that the increasing interest in the Red Planet has a
  dark side: what he calls "crap". This "crap" is the astonishing
  theory that there is more to Mars than what official science
  tells us and that the space agencies involved in its exploration
  are covering something up. The most prominent figure in
  alternative Martian investigation is Richard Hoagland and Ellison
  doesn't mince his words when he mentions Hoagland: "I hate him so
  much!" He an unequivocal and very cynical believer in the Strong
  Hoaglandic Principle, that the man is a money-grabbing
  blackguard, pure and simple. He's talking nonsense and he knows
  it, but doesn't care because it sells books and DVD's! (The Weak
  Hoaglandic Principle states that he's talking nonsense, but that
  he is honestly deluded and really thinks that what he's saying is
  true.) Ellison denies that a conspiracy is possible because
  there's more than one space agency involved nowadays, not just
  NASA. The European Space Agency and others would have to be in on
  the plot for it to work; too many people would have to know,
  making the conspiracy unacceptably top-heavy. (This is one of the
  criticisms of the Moon-landing hoax theory too, not a criticism I
  accept for reasons I state below). The idea that the data from
  Mars is subject to censorship is, according to Ellison, wrong
  because the signal from Mars Express and other relay satellites
  in Mars orbit is made available unedited on the Net just 30
  minutes after it arrives. There is no human interference in the
  data-stream. To demonstrate this he put up a photo on the
  projector screen that had just been sent from Spirit. Apparently
  if you have the right receiver you can pick up the signal
  yourself at home, bypassing all the usual channels; somebody in
  Belgium has done just that! He also demonstrated that the notion
  that the pictures taken on Mars prove that NASA are lying about
  the atmosphere being thin and poisonous, and that the planet
  really has a thick, breathable atmosphere, are misunderstandings
  based on the various effects of photograph processing. For
  example in some of the Mars photos the sky looks blue, but this
  is simply because the "Pancam" cameras with which the Spirit
  Rover and other probes are equipped have a separate blue-filtered
  field. This part of his research is very persuasive and it became
  obvious to me that some of the ideas of the Martian cover-up
  based on photo-colour are wrong; here's a good example of the
  kind of notions he debunked:
  http://uk.youtube.com/watch?v=DZU_pPdNedc&feature=related
  I'm sold! They are genuine photos. (but whether they are genuine
  photos of the real Martian surface is another matter; as is
  whether the Martian surface depicted is both real and natural;
  but that's a long story, beyond the immediate scope of this
  article!) However I don't share Ellison's confidence that a
  conspiracy is out of the question just because many different
  space agencies from many different nations are involved.
  Corruption is far more insidious, durable and widespread than is
  commonly known. I have witnessed firsthand, in very benign-
   looking institutions, the most appalling deceit, destruction and
  social violence concealed under a frighteningly thin veneer. I
  was also dismayed at how willing so many people are to turn a
  blind eye. The "just get on with your job and don't rock the
  boat" ethic is a commonly-upheld one indeed. The recent organized
  child abuse scandals in North Wales and the Channel Islands are a
  good example. Some space agencies also have a few skeletons in
  their cupboard, and as far as NASA is concerned it is an ossuary!
  NASA works on classified military operations and always has done,
  from launching spy satellites to "Star Wars" experiments. They've
  employed some very dodgy characters and given fame and
  respectability to people who really belong in jail! In my opinion
  NASA has not earned the people's trust.
  Ellison then went on to address some other Martian scoops that he
  thinks have been blown out of all proportion by the media, like
  the "Sedimentary Sasquatch". I didn't know it was called that,
  but I've heard about it and written about it myself:
  http://hpanwo.blogspot.com/2008/01/prood-of-alien-on-mars.html .
  With the passing of time since I wrote the article, this object
  looks less convincing. It could be simply a "cloud-teddy"; our
  brains' visual centre tends to seek out recognizable shapes in
  random chaotic images. The continued media interest in gimmicky


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m22-003.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:20]
Skeptics In The Pub

  curiosities like this actually begins to feel a bit like a
  "public relations exercise" to me. What better way to make people
  reject any real Martian anomalies than to focus their attention
  on something so obviously unimpressive and easy to disprove?
  Other anomalous objects that have been spotted in Mars photos are
  actually just parts of the spacecraft that have been jettisoned
  in their descent, like the heat-shield and parachute.
  For a while I thought Ellison was going to avoid the most famous
  alternative Mars investigation subject of all: the Face on Mars,
  but he didn't disappoint. He views the Face in a very similar way
  to the "Sedimentary Sasquatch", a cloud-teddy; and to support his
  opinion, he put up pics of many other face-like objects on the
  surface of Mars that none of the "conspiracy theorists" point to.
  The Face dates back to the 1976 Viking mission, where it was
  spotted at a press conference. Since then more recent pictures of
  the Face have been published by modern craft like the Mars Global
  Surveyor; or at least NASA have told us that's what they are.
  Here are some of them:
  http://tinyurl.com/55plrr
  It looks a lot less face-like and more like a cloud- teddy now;
  Ellison thinks that's all it is. However, I once again disagree
  with Ellison's assertion that this closes the case. The original
  Viking images were subjected to fractal analysis, a military
  system that was used on spy-plane and satellite photos to spot
  enemy tanks in the Gulf War. The system is specifically designed
  to eliminate the natural cloud-teddy function of human vision. It
  concluded that the Face was the most unnatural object for
  hundreds of miles around. Other researchers have also analyzed
  the more recent Face pictures and disagreed that it is natural.
  This vid is very interesting. I jumped out of my seat when they
  fist showed the Face!:
  http://tinyurl.com/6y9lnz
  "The Face on Mars is not artificial!" exclaimed Ellison "This is
  what artificial objects look like!" and he showed us a Google
  Earth picture of the Egyptian Pyramids. But I wonder what the
  Pyramids will look like in the future. If the Face on Mars is the
  creation of an extinct Martian civilization then it is extremely
  old, billions of years old, maybe even predating life on Earth
  itself, let alone terrestrial human civilization! I wonder how
  "artificial" the Pyramids will look after a few more millennia of
  environmental weathering. So you see, it's not a suitable
  comparison. As far as Hoagland goes I personally believe in the
  "Super-Weak Hoaglandic Principle"; in that I believe he's genuine
  about what he says, what's more he's not talking complete
  nonsense either. But I certainly don't go along with all his
  views. I concur with Ellison's opinion that "Topogly" is all
  bollocks. You can generate significant mathematical constants out
  of almost anything, so long as you have enough points to link
  angles between! But there are some interesting "coincidences"
  with Cydonia which involve far more basic mathematical geography
  (or to be pedantic: "Areography") and deserve further study in my
  view: The complex lies on the 120th Meridian, taking Olympus Mons
  as the prime one; that's exactly one third of the way round the
  planet. The whole complex around the Face matches the layout of
  ancient monuments on Earth, like the Avebury circle and its
  environs in Wiltshire; the resemblance is uncanny! Of course you
  could put it down to "coincidence", but if you do that why not do
  the same for the Mona Lisa? You could claim it wasn't really a
  portrait at all; it's just that Leonardo spilled a few pots of
  paint onto a canvas by accident! That's the big problem with
  Coincidence Theory: where's the cut-off point?
  Whatever Ellison and anyone else asserts, the truth is that there
  is an opaque veil that covers human activity in space and that
  when the authorities tell us what space is like and show us data
  to support their claims, we have to take their word for it to a
  large extent. We can't see what's going on out on Mars with our
  own eyes! We have to rely on authorities and trust them. I've
  stated above that I think that space authorities have the means
  and opportunity to conduct a hoax. How? And what is there to
  cover up? Well, I can't elaborate on that in this article. But
  seeing as they have a means and opportunity, do they have the
  motive as well? Well, imagine for a moment the effect it would
  have on our society if it was announced that we had absolute
  proof of intelligent extraterrestrial life, even if it was
  extinct; what would happen to our political, religious and social


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m22-003.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:20]
Skeptics In The Pub

  structures? There are some very powerful people in the world
  whose only mission is to hang on to that power at all costs.
  Public acknowledgement that intelligent life "Out There" is real
  could threaten it in many ways; and there are psychological PR
  studies that say this in as many words, like the Brookings
  Institute Report of 1961. I'll be writing a lot about that in the
  future. Let's assume for a moment that official History is
  correct and that the Mariner and Viking missions really were
  humanity's first encounter with the Red Planet (I'm not certain
  of that they were, but that's a story for another time!). The
  pics come back showing the Face on Mars, NASA say: "Oh dear! What
  are we going to do!? Everyone can see a relic of alien
  intelligence!" They can't airbrush it out in future publications,
  nor can they from pictures from future missions because anyone
  looking would spot the Face's absence, so the solution?: downplay
  it and seed false data and disinformation.
  I had a chat with Ellison after the lecture and got on rather
  well with him, but this is probably because I held back a lot of
  my opinions! He said: "Mars is an amazing and intriguing enough
  place already without inventing secret conspiracies about it."
  That's true... not that this is a reason to declare that there
  can't possibly be any conspiracies when there could be, but I see
  what he means. He is currently reading one of my favourite
  novels. The Mars Trilogy by Kim Stanley Robinson
  http://tinyurl.com/6r39p8
  Unlike me, Ellison is only interested in the nuts-and-bolts
  scientific aspect to the story whereas I also appreciate its
  exploration of sociology and politics. It's an amazing sci-fi
  book that is set in official future History (Just in case
  anyone's thinking that I don't read normal books!). Unlike my
  first visit to SITP I managed to strike up some conversations
  with the other patrons. I had a good chat with a nice bloke
  called Colin and also met a friendly fellow called Jack of Kent
  who runs his own blog:
  http://jackofkent.blogspot.com/
  He's posted comments on my first SITP article, see above. He
  explained to me that the reason people were so reserved and
  standoffish at the last SITP was because that's what Londoners
  tend to be; it's a habit. I can accept that after having a much
  more social experience there this time. I also admit that I have
  suffered a bit from paranoia and prejudice because of the Skepper
  who's been harassing me for the last three years! The latest SITP
  has reassured me that not all Skeppers are like him! I'll look
  forward to the one next month and hope I can go along!

  In some small way by confiding in me [me for christ sakes] and me

  actually had heard of these experiences before.
  We can make up all of the buzz words we want about this
  phenomenon, run down all of the blind trails we care to invent,

                                         Truth Is Out There And Science Can Prove It
  From: Sheryl Gottschall <gottscha.nul>
  Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 10:39:25 +1000
  Archived: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 09:57:00 -0400
  Subject: Truth Is Out There And Science Can Prove It

  Source: The Age - Melbourne,Victoria, Australia
  http://tinyurl.com/6afxqt
  August 21, 2008
  [Link to video]
  The Truth Is Out There - And Science Can Prove It
  One of the myths Michael Shermer is quick to debunk is that
  being a sceptic means he is a non-believer. "I believe in lots of
  things", he says, "just show me the evidence."
  Author, scientist and founder of the US Skeptics Society, Dr
  Shermer would like to see everyone exercise "an ounce of
  scepticism".
  From alien sightings to 9/11 conspiracy theories, he says, many
  topics cry out for a sceptical mind. "If you claim you have Big
  Foot, if you claim you have an alien from another planet, show me
  the body."
  A fundamentalist Christian during his high school years, Dr
  Shermer became a sceptic as he trained to become a scientist.
  That's because science is scepticism, he says, and vice versa.
  Dr Shermer believes UFO sightings are sightings of objects such
  as weather balloons or blimps and he links "alien abductions" to
  sleep disorders.
  Dr Shermer will give presentations as part of National Science
  Week, which runs until Sunday.

Re: Abduction Explanations


  >Bottom line is, it's real. Just because our sciences haven't or
  >won't resolve the matter doesn't mean it's less real. Sure some
  >accounts are fantasy or downright fibs but there's reality there
  >without question.
  <snip>
  At the apparent risk, considering the discussion so far in this
  thread, of being considered some kind of "heretic's heretic," I
  would like to venture a few questions that some here may think
  simply rhetorical, but truly are not :
  What if, despite all the anecdotal accounts, there are actually
  no alien abductions occurring? What if, rather than assuming
  extraterrestrials, be they grays or otherwise, there is not just
  one, but a number of other phenomena, some known, and others
  unknown, as yet, that may account for what is generally
  considered evidence for "alien abductions"? What other kinds of
  explanations, evidence, or data is there to necessarily think we
  are, absolutely, dealing with aliens in these kinds of events and
  reports? Could we, by making either assumptions or some forms of
  conclusion, or even just belief, be diverting ourselves here by
  not considering alternative explanations or possibilities?
  For example, regarding implants: can someone here cite for me an
  analysis or peer-reviewed paper that involves investigation and
  examination of any implant ever removed from a person that is
  undeniably, or in some scientifically provable way, not either
  prosaic or the result of some inadvertent, accidental, or human-
  created object? Is there any evidence of any implant that has
  either construction, materials, or other evidence of something
  truly non-terrestrial, whether natural in composition or
  artificial (in the sense a person may have created it)?
  I would honestly like to know what, if any, evidence exists that
  a serious researcher has or could hold up or use as a basis to
  say, "Here is a proof of an extraterrestrial or alien artifact"
  and also be able to say empirically how and why.

  Steve Sawyer

                                            Lights Fuel Calder Valley UFO Speculation
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 11:12:00 -0400
  Archived: Fri, 22 Aug 2008 11:12:00 -0400
  Subject: Lights Fuel Calder Valley UFO Speculation



  Source: Hebdenbridge Today - Hebden Bridge, UK
  http://tinyurl.com/6jk5t7
  23 August 2008

  Mystery Lights Fuel UFO Speculations Throughout Calder Valley
  It's not the first time that Calder Valley residents have seen
  mysterious lights in the night sky, but a number of sightings
  over the past few weeks are remarkably similar in description.
  Between the end of July and this week householders up and down
  the length of the valley, from Todmorden to Mytholmroyd, have
  described seeing silently moving bright yellow or orange lights
  make their way across the sky in a way that does not seem like
  conventional aircraft.
  And another possible explanation, that they are hot air balloons,
  seems unlikely because the lights are seen in the night sky.
  First residents in the Burnley Road area of Todmorden saw
  patterns of lights on the night of Saturday, July 26.
  Gemma Kipping said family guests were visiting. "Some of them
  left before the others and were walking home but rang us after
  they had set off to say 'there are aliens above your house!'
  "So we went outside and I saw three bright orange lights moving
  uniformly with what looked like a straggler at the end. The three
  at the front looked like a triangle effect. They weren't making
  any noise," she said.
  While the family watched, a dozen or so customers from the nearby
  Hare and Hounds pub on Burnley Road, Todmorden, were also
  watching the lights move across the sky, said Gemma.
  "I didn't know what they were," she added. "The ideal explanation
  would have been that they were a hot air balloon, but surely not
  in the dark?"
  Similar lights were also seen on the night of Saturday, August 2,
  at 11.15 pm by other Burnley Road residents including Sylvia
  Sinclair, who contacted the newspaper after reading about similar
  descriptions of lights in the sky from residents of Mytholmroyd
  in our sister paper the Evening Courier.
  Sylvia explained that friends were leaving her home at Lineholme
  when they all saw the lights, which appeared to be coming over to
  the Whirlaw side of the valley.
  "They came in twos and looked like big orange lights. They were
  making no noise and there were six, in pairs. The last one seemed
  to float over," she said.
  Like Gemma, Sylvia wondered if they could be balloons but thought


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m22-016.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:26]
Lights Fuel Calder Valley UFO Speculation

  they were too high for that.
  "While we were looking a teenager came down the street and said
  they were out at the Hare and Hounds looking at the lights. They
  were just silent, going slowly across the sky," she said.
  The next sighting of strange lights came further down the valley,
  on Monday, August 11, in the Mytholmroyd area.
  Cragg Vale resident Chris Granger told the Courier he was shocked
  to see six strange lights for two to three minutes before they
  disappeared, emerging from the cloud base in pairs and moving
  towards Hebden Bridge.
  The ex-RAF avionics technician said: "They moved in a very
  erratic manner and did not display the flight characteristics of
  a conventional aircraft. Nor did they display the normal lighting
  array of a conventional aircraft - flashing white strobe and red
  and green navigation lights."
  Cleveley Gardens residents Peter and Marion Ackroyd also saw
  something spooky.
  They also wondered if they were balloons but thought they were
  going too fast, in addition to the lack of any engine noise.
  Earlier this week Mytholmroyd resident Mark Jeffreys said his
  wife Mandy called him and sons Matthew and Liam outside where
  they saw seven orange lights coming over, two together, another
  two, then one and then a final two.
  Mandy said: "It couldn't have been helicopters because they were
  orange lights, not white. I've never seen anything like it, but
  Mark said he thought he'd seen something similar when he was a
  kid."
  The Calder Valley is home to one of the world's most famous cases
  involving Unidentified Flying Objects, that of Todmorden's Alan
  Godfrey, then a serving policeman.
  Alan's case, which dates back to 1980, was examined by a Channel
  5 documentary only weeks ago. While on mobile patrol in Burnley
  Road he described and sketched in his police notebook an object
  which appeared to be hovering over the road.
  He then cannot consciously remember anything for a period of
  time, coming round further down the road. Under hypnosis with a
  senior police officer present he described being taken aboard an
  alien spacecraft and examined - but remembers none of this
  consciously.
  Police officers from two different forces reported seeing an
  unexplained object zip across the valley on the night in question
  and the amount of information officially logged made it one of
  the best documented cases in the world, and one which continues
  to fascinate people who discover it.
  Can anyone explain the latest series of so far unexplainable
  sightings?

  >Hi Frank,
  >Can you provide details on the "legal precedence" given to
  >deathbed confessions or affidavits? It was interesting to note
  >that a Google search of "Deathbed Affidavits" brought up a full
  >page of links related to the Walter Haut statement. But these
  >indicated an increased interest in Roswell as a result of his
  >claims, not that the case was being given any greater credence.
  An exception to the hearsay rules is the 'dying declaration'. The
  precedence would fill volumes. I won’t bore the List, but what is
  relevant is that any statement made outside of court is usually
  considered hearsay and therefore not admissible. The hearsay
  exception is mainly used in criminal trials but has been expanded
  and used in other cases.
  The medieval English courts had the principle of "Nemo moriturus
  praesumitur mentiri", meaning a dying person is not presumed to
  lie. I believe this theory originated during the 12th-century
  reign of Richard the Lionhearted, when Christianity was gaining
  influence. Since most U.S. law is derived from the body of
  English common law, it is understandable that we follow the
  precedence.
  However, the rule is not applied uniformly in different
  jurisdictions. To my knowledge all jurisdictions allow the
  exception but some restrict its use in some form or another. It
  is allowed under the U.S. Federal Rules of Evidence and under the
  State of Florida’s Rules of Evidence, being the two I am
  familiar.
  It is safe to say that present-day courts follow the medieval
  precedence. In recent years, many judges have used their
  discretionary powers to admit dying declarations that probably
  shouldn't have been aired in court. The bottom line is that it
  has weigh when admitted. For whatever reason, judges and juries


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m22-018.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:27]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  seem to feel that a dying person is less likely to lie.

  Regards,
  Frank

  by
  Matt Cunningham
  Could the Northern Territory be under attack from an armada of
  UFOs?
  The Northern Territory News has been inundated in recent weeks
  with readers' pictures of possible UFO sightings.
  The objects captured on camera have ranged from dark disks flying
  in broad daylight to strange lights glowing in the night sky.
  Roger Perner, 52, of the Hunter Valley in NSW, was taking
  pictures of eagles at Policeman's Point in Timber Creek on the
  Victoria River last month when he noticed a strange object in one
  of the shots.
  "As soon as I dropped the camera I looked around everywhere and
  there was nothing in the sky," he said.
  Mr Perner said he had believed in extra-terrestrial life since
  seeing a strange object in the sky in Queensland about 30 years
  ago.
  "It was miles and miles away and as big as a football," he said.
  He said he had no idea what the object he photographed last month
  was.
  "It wasn't there when I took the camera away from my eye but it
  was there when I took the photo," he said.
  In March, Ruth Palmer, 27, of Rosebery, Palmerston, took a
  picture of her husband Richard Magree in front of the Devils
  Marbles, near infamous UFO town Wycliffe Well.
  When she looked at the photograph she noticed a strange object in
  the sky flying above her husband's shoulder.
  "You don't want to think you are crazy, and I don't want to be
  one of those crazies, but I thought, being near Wycliffe Well,
  who knows what it is?"
  Stephen Jones, of Alice Springs, was also baffled when he
  photographed strange lights in the sky near Banka Banka, while
  driving from Darwin to Alice Springs in February.

  weight than the testimony of living witnesses or experts? I can't
  think of any; or find any reference to such cases, but it would
  be interesting to see how they arrived at that decision.

  >>Hi Frank,
  >>Can you provide details on the "legal precedence" given to
  >>deathbed confessions or affidavits? It was interesting to note
  >>that a Google search of "Deathbed Affidavits" brought up a full

  >>indicated an increased interest in Roswell as a result of his

  >An exception to the hearsay rules is the 'dying declaration'. The
  >precedence would fill volumes. I won=E2=80=99t bore the List, but what is=
  >relevant is that any statement made outside of court is usually
  >considered hearsay and therefore not admissible. The hearsay
  >exception is mainly used in criminal trials but has been expanded
  >and used in other cases.
  It is a hearsay exception to allow dying declarations into
  evidence, not to give them any extra weight. Dying declarations
  get a foot in the door at a court trial where they would
  otherwise be excluded as hearsay, not a free pass to overwhelm
  all other evidence as if some kind of conclusive truth. As one
  law review has pointed out, "The desire to justify one's own
  actions, to have the approbation of one's friends, moreover, may
  lead to conscious or unconscious falsification even in extremis
  [near death]."
  Dying declarations are only allowed as testimony about the cause
  or circumstances of the witness' impending death, not on any ole
  subject under the sun! A dying homicide victim who states on
  their deathbed that "I saw John Doe shoot me" is the kind of


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m23-006.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:31]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  "dying declaration" contemplated in law, _not_ "Roswell was an
  alien crash."
  The dying declaration must be of percipient testimony, something
  the dying person actually witnessed, not their mere opinion.
  Dying declarations are not universally allowed in all types of
  court proceedings. That fact hardly makes dying declarations into
  some kind of superevidence whose power of credibility overwhelms
  other categories of evidence.
  Furthermore there are criteria that must be followed in order to
  allow a dying declaration into evidence, besides the fact it must
  be a homicide case involving the dying person.
  The dying declaration has to be the person's "last words," not
  something where the person has months or years of future ahead.
  If the dying person has the slightest hope of recovery, no matter
  how unreasonable, the supposed "dying declaration" is not
  admissible into evidence. Judges are never going to allow
  declarations from someone who is years away from death to be
  admitted into evidence without cross-examination by the other
  party's counsel.
  Furthermore, if a dying declarant was available for cross-
  examination but the proponents of the declaration did not make
  the person known and available for cross-examination, the dying
  declaration will be inadmissible.
  The dying declarant must also be competent and of sound mind when
  making the declaration, otherwise the declaration is
  inadmissible.
  I can imagine that if there was ever any conceivable UFO-related
  actual dying declaration that the other side would immediately
  pounce on the UFO aspects to argue that the dying declarant was
  therefore _not_ of sound mind. Maybe they would prevail on that
  argument, maybe not. But it would suddenly become a key issue.
  Some studies have shown that dying persons are often like the
  oxygen-deprived at high altitudes. Their mental functioning is
  impaired.
  >The medieval English courts had the principle of "Nemo moriturus
  >praesumitur mentiri", meaning a dying person is not presumed to
  >lie. I believe this theory originated during the 12th-century
  >reign of Richard the Lionhearted, when Christianity was gaining
  >influence. Since most U.S. law is derived from the body of
  >English common law, it is understandable that we follow the
  >precedence.
  Cite me current case law recognizing this medieval common law
  principle applies to make dying declarations of _heavier_weight_
  than other categories of evidence. Non-cross-examined testimony
  such as dying declarations are considered inherently
  untrustworthy, and only this one exception is allowed under
  strict controls. It may have a dramatic impact on a trial but it
  is a prejudicial impact.
  Needless to say, but I'll say it anyway, using tricks of legal
  precedence to try to bootstrap some kind of "proof" of Roswell
  does not make it testable _scientific_ evidence. It's a
  _political_ argument, not scientific evidence. A political
  argument tries to sway people and can be based on sound
  evidentiary grounds but there is no requirement for such and
  usually it is based on appeals to prejudice and popular biases.

  Brad Sparks

  Origin of an artifact is known when the point of origin is
  observed.
  Markings on an artifact or statements made by occupants could be
  deceptions.
  US B-29's flying into Alaska at the end of WWII had US markings
  but their point of origin was Russia, not the US, because they
  were part of a Lend-Lease deal. Relying on the artifact's
  markings instead of radio and radar observations of the actual
  point of origin would have been misleading, resulting in a false
  conclusion.
  One cannot still say, "Well, the US origin would not have been
  entirely wrong because the B-29's were indeed manufactured in the
  US." Later USAF war planners believed the Soviets might paint
  their Tu-4 Bear copies of the B-29 to look like USAF B-29's with
  (false) USAF markings, so they could slip through our air
  defenses. So if such "B-29's" had been observed their point of
  origin would have been completely false if based on the "USAF"
  markings. Again, the artifact alone does not give proof of its
  point of origin.
  In order to know that a UFO came from, for example, Zeta Reticuli
  2, one would have to observe it coming from Zeta Reticuli 2. If a
  landed UFO had a marking painted on its side saying "Made in the
  Zeta Reticuli 2 system," we would not believe it even aside from
  the absurdity of being written in English. If an abductee is told
  by an alleged alien "We come from the Zeta Reticuli 2 system," we
  have no more reason to believe it than if the statement had been
  painted on the outer hull. It is not a direct observation of a

  Might this metal pin have been something like an old dental crown
  post? These are pins made of steel or titanium and an image here
  shows one with an axial ratio of about 13:1.
  http://www.agokadental.com/images/rc_img16.jpg
  Apparently the lifetime of a crown tooth is reckoned as 5-15
  years and decay can continue in the remnant root even after
  implantation. Is it possible that nonexistent or negligent
  dentistry after a crown broke off could have allowed the steel
  post to remain in place after which it migrated through the gum
  over the course of some years?
  I'm not saying that this supportable, but it's an obvious
  speculation. I don't see any discussion of the possibility here.
  Has it been checked and ruled out?
  One sure way of doing that would be to show that the object did
  not have the materials characteristics of a dental crown post.
  But there's no further information given on the object removed.
  Results of an analysis are said to be pending and will be "made
  available at a later date". There is no date at all on the web
  page, but the date of the surgery was apparently Dec 2003 so it
  could be over four years old. Where are the results of this
  analysis?
  Clicking on "Articles" produces the NIDS/New Mexico Tech report
  on other objects reportedly removed surgically from other
  subjects in 1995. It says that Dr Leir had fully documented the
  links in the chain of transfer of evidence from his operation to
  NIDS which is reassuring (although the nature of this procedure
  isn't described - or if it was checkable other than by reference
  to Dr Leir). Assuming the chain of evidence from the subject to
  the lab is indeed sound then this is more interesting.
  The analysis report (which a bit easier to read on the NIDS site
  http://www.nidsci.org/articles/metal/metal.html
  although I notice that the photomicrographs missing from the
  Alienscalpel site are frustratingly not shown here either)
  says:
  "In an attempt to learn more about the iron, or iron-alloy core
  of these samples, traditional metallography using an optical
  microscope was performed. The ground and polished cross-section
  of sample T1,2-B was etched using "Nital" (HNO_3 & methanol). The
  fact that nital etched the sample very quickly affirms the
  presence of an iron-rich alloy. Etching revealed a very fine (too
  fine to produce a good photograph) maze-like pattern of light and
  dark regions, reminiscent of a slowly-cooled eutectic
  composition. Although the microstructure did not reveal a
  "classic" Pearlite structure, the system is presumed to be iron-
  carbon, with the dark phase being perhaps cementite (Fe_3C) in a
  matrix of ferrite (alpha-Fe). A high percentage of finely
  dispersed carbon may account for the very high hardness (VH=821)
  as reported earlier. Ferrite is favored over austenite (gamma-Fe)
  due to the fact that the sample core is apparently
  ferromagnetic."
  "Summary
  "Sample T1,2 can be described as needle or lamellar in shape,
  with a predominantly iron core and a non-conducting, dark gray-
  black coating. This coating or surface layer material has Fe, Ca,
  P, Cl and very possibly some lighter elements (i.e. C, O) as its
  constituents. The phase analysis via x-ray diffraction was not
  absolutely conclusive due to the extremely small sample size,
  however the best fit to the obtained pattern suggests Anapaite,
  Ca_2Fe(PO_4_)2H_2O, Goethite, FeO(OH), iron phosphide, FeP_4, and
  phosphorus oxide, P_2O_5, as likely phases. The microstructure of
  the core (polished and etched) as observed under an optical
  microscope resembles an iron rich alloy with large amounts of
  carbon, probably in the form of iron carbide. The iron is likely
  to be alpha-Fe with a body-centered-cubic packing (bcc structure)
  since the samples are magnetized. The hardness of this core
  material is very high, in the neighborhood of high carbon tool
  steels."




http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m25-002.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:34]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  In short, analysis showed a thin needle-like eutectic iron alloy
  with a bcc crystal structure (i.e., steel) coated in a layer of
  minerals. The metal core was "iron, with major quantities of
  silicon, phosphorous, molybdenum, chlorine, sodium, calcium and a
  trace of copper". Copper, molybdenum, phosphorus and silicon are
  characteristic additives in high-strength and hard steels.
  Chlorine could maybe come from ferrous chloride which is a waste
  product of a hydrochloric acid "pickling" process used to de-
  scale carbon steel prior to processing. I dont know about rthe
  sodium, but really this all seems conventional to me. At least,
  if there's anything unconventional it must be some subtle
  metallurgical detail of mixture ratios, nothing that screams
  "exotic materials technology" or "unknown physics". I see mention
  of some rough surface or shape defects that sound like corrosion
  or something; but other than that we have what sounds like a
  fragment of a steel needle or similar.
  The mineral coating was a calcium phosphate (in a phase thought
  possibly to be Anapaite, or hydrated calcium iron phosphate),
  Goethite (an iron oxydroxide) and phosphorous oxide. Phosphate
  minerals are very closely related to the composition of human
  bone and teeth, and for that reason calcium phosphates similar to
  Anapaite are widely used as "bioceramic" coatings on dental and
  other surgical implants and as bone fillers because they bind
  with the bone, and they are also used in toothpastes as carriers
  to transport fluorine atoms into the tooth mineral.
  http://www.azom.com/details.asp?ArticleID=107
  A possibly related factor is that Anapaite whilst usually
  classified as a mineral, is regarded by some as not being a true
  mineral because it may have a partially organic origin, being
  found in association with fossil shell remains.
  http://www.galleries.com/minerals/phosphat/anapaite/anapaite.htm
  The common implant coating material is hydroxyapatite, a calcium
  phosphate phase closely related to anapaite but containing no
  iron. However when it is bound to the iron alloy it appears that
  other related phosphate phases may form:
  "The plasma spraying process produces coatings on the order of
  40-60 micrometer thick. The chemistry and structure of the
  coatings are similar to those of HA [hydroxyapatite]; however,
  the plasma spraying process will result in the formation of
  amorphous and other Ca-P [calcium phosphate] phases in the
  resulting coatings"
  http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=4273826
  So again I'm not convinced that there is strong evidence of
  exotic materials or exotic technology in the mineral coating
  which looks similar to the types of coatings used on conventional
  medical steel implants especially those like pins and posts
  (dental or otherwise) designed to bond to bone. It isn't at all
  clear what part of a person's anatomy these samples were
  supposedly taken from, or what the subjects' history of medical
  proceedures might have been. I'd like to see a lot more
  information about the samples, the procedures and the subjects
  before concluding there is evidemce of exotic alien or exotic
  terrestrial technology. Maybe this information is out there -
  somewhere? But why not put it here - or at the very least links
  or references to it - on what Dr Leir promotes as
  "the only website dedicated to the victims of the Alien Abduction
  Phenomenon. - click here to help support the research"
  In the place of useful scientific information what we get are
  book and DVD promos, an Online Store and an announcement that the
  "internationally famous" neice of Hollywood legend Carmen Miranda
  has been signed as Assistant Executive Producer on a motion
  picture called 'Earth's Original Sin', to fund which Dr Leir
  invites $500.00 "donations" in return for a "gift" of 1/8% gross
  profits after 20 years.

  Also under "Articles" there's one by a reporter, describing two
  other operations he witnessed (via video monitor) in 1995 where
  Dr Leir apparently removed unidentified small objects from the
  big toe of one subject and the hand of another. According to the
  reporter:

Re: Abduction Explanations

  she was located in our galaxy then where her "captors" were from
  would have had little significance for her. These spacefarers,
  obviously, would not have Zeta 1 or Zeta 2 Reticuli as the names
  for their home planets if they are their home planets. Chances
  are that at the time Betty could not identify her own Solar
  system if it was pointed out to her.
  Is it not an assumption that the map she saw was even germane to
  the origin of those who abducted her? Why assume this map was
  associated with their parent planet. Come to my home and you will
  see maps laying around in my office. One laying open right now is
  an airnav chart of New Mexico. If I abducted some tourists and
  brought them here blindfolded and they saw that map, should they
  assume that I am from New Mexico?
  Having done a lot of navigation in my time it doesn't make sense
  to me that you would need a star map of where you came from.
  Navigation is done piecemeal using lots of local maps and
  references along the way. These map references are verified as
  you come up to and pass them then on to the next reference.
  Unless the map Betty "saw" was just hanging there as a picture
  like us having a map of the solar system on the wall of some
  super space ship for aesthetic or nostalgic reasons, I see no
  need of it.
  But I can't discount the possibility of it's being a depiction of
  their own home turf as seen from the general direction of Earth.
  If Marjory Fish did generally match it up it was from our
  viewpoint on the outer edge of a sphere 36 light years in
  diameter with ZR1 and ZR2 as the center. Move around that sphere
  and the positions of the stars would shift.
  Any intelligence capable of star travel is going to have some
  mind boggling navigation devices at their fingertips; super
  computers we could only imagine. The whole ships systems would
  likely be an entity of it's own with the intelligence to travel
  to the stars. The biologicals on board would just be along for
  the ride. And it sure wouldn't be some little 60 foot diameter
  "saucer".
  I don't subscribe to the point to point theory, meaning that the
  extraterrestrials in question in the Hill case came from there to
  here purposefully-particularly not in some little craft. Anyway
  the odds for the former happening are astronomical.
  Like anything else - i.e. evolution for example - pure chance
  seems to have a better shot at being the case rather than some
  discovery of our little planet from their's however there is the
  possibility of of some sophisticated determination of our
  location and other scientific evidence of a chance of life here
  through the use of direct observation [like a super Hubble-
  bending light through gravity - a manufactured gravity lens ?]
  and subsequent spectro-analysis. There wasn't time [25 years from
  the first video transmissions] to receive VHF/UHF emissions from
  Earth 36 light years away and then travel here to check it out.
  The mind boggles at the possibility of having the technology in
  place that could permit these space farers to leave at a moments
  notice just to check out seemingly intelligent/coherent signals
  coming from a singular point in space.
  In the Hill case Betty might have just seen a map-if it was a
  map-of the last place visited, or the next stop on their mission.
  Chances are these abductors-if extraterrestrial-have been in our
  locale for decades, centuries of millennia.
  If the ETH is indeed the right "H", I'm more comfortable with the
  theory that some extraterrestrial presence is here on outpost
  duty and have been for a very long time. I've expounded before on
  my belief that if there is anything to the ETH then this planet
  was probably discovered while ancient intelligences were
  exploring the outer reaches of this galaxy. I have not read or
  seen any other theory to change my mind.

  Don Ledger

  >have to take two flights from Fredericton to get anywhere and to
  >get home. But my origin was the airport from which I left on the
  >first flight, not the last one.
  We know that an airliner came from Tokyo because hundreds of
  passengers, flight crew, air traffic controllers armed with radar
  and navigation instruments verify that it came from Tokyo, was
  seen visually and on radar taking off from Tokyo. We accept
  evidence like this every day without requiring special
  investigations.
  But if the issue is an important one or subject to controversy,
  then a higher standard of investigation is required to verify
  that there were indeed direct observations that the airliner came
  from Tokyo and not somewhere else. But direct observations are
  still needed.
  This is not a silly or frivolous issue. Suppose our hypothetical
  Tokyo airliner became an instrument of mass destruction, a weapon
  of terrorism. In that case every aspect of its flight path and
  departure would be thoroughly investigated and not entrusted to


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m25-004.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:35]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  merely looking up and uncritically believing a flight schedule.
  Suppose a terrorist showed a passenger aboard the Tokyo flight a
  navigational map showing the flight seemingly coming from North
  Korea not Tokyo based on the passenger's limited understanding of
  geography and brevity of seeing the map, and phones a message to
  someone on the ground saying that.
  Would we accept such highly inferential evidence and say that the
  airliner really came from N Korea, maybe after diversion from
  Tokyo, and that N Korea should be attacked in retaliation? Or
  would we still demand direct observational evidence before making
  some serious decisions with enormous consequences?
  Suppose a nuclear explosion occurs in the US. It is considered an
  attack of some kind. Who was responsible and how do we know? If
  radar and satellites track the flight path of an ICBM or a cruise
  missile all the way from launch in Russia or China or North Korea
  or Iran or wherever, then we know the point of origin from direct
  observation. This does not depend on the markings seen on the
  missile, which could be falsified (yes, cruise missiles can be
  slow enough that fighter pilots can come alongside and see
  markings).
  Suppose we have no radar or sensor observations of any missile or
  vehicle impacting at the time of the nuclear explosion. If we
  have an airtight sensor grid then we can deduce that it was most
  likely a terrorist nuclear bomb smuggled in overland, but we
  really won't know for sure because we won't have direct
  observation of the bomb's point of origin. We just have
  inferences, maybe guesses. Maybe it was a stealth cruise missile
  that slipped through our air defense sensor array, maybe we
  really don't have any way of knowing whether it was or was not a
  stealth missile or a bomb on the ground, without direct
  observations of launch at the point of origin.
  Maybe it was a terrorist theft of a US nuclear weapon, so the
  bomb actually "came from here" (not so absurd a possibility after
  the recent Minot AFB incident where the supposedly error-proof
  nuclear inventory system lost track of 6 nuclear-tipped cruise
  missiles). In the 1950's there was a lot of fear about accidental
  nuclear detonations before fail-safe systems were fully matured,
  but maybe accidental explosion is still a remote possibility.
  In that scenario, we cannot tell if the bomb came "from here" or
  "came from elsewhere" and we cannot tell if it is "elsewhere"
  without knowing for sure exactly "where" this "elsewhere" place
  represents, by directly observing its point of origin, not by
  inferring it or guessing at it. (The analogy to the UFO situation
  should be obvious.) Was it a terrorist nuke smuggled in from
  _elsewhere_, or a terrorist nuke assembled from parts stolen
  _here_, or a complete bomb stolen _here_, or a bomb accidentally
  detonated _here_ and not coming from "elsewhere" at all?
  The only way we can be certain the bomb came from elsewhere is if
  it was observed being launched from elsewhere, in China or Iran
  or wherever -- likewise with a UFO's point of origin. Everything
  else is lesser degrees of certainty, in reality just
  probabilities of inference and at the lowest end, sheer guesses.
  Suppose we have a partial radar track of the very end of the
  flight path of the missile just before impact in the US. Suppose
  back projection leads to a point of origin in Asia. But both
  ICBM's with MARV (maneuverable reentry vehicle) warheads and
  cruise missiles are maneuverable.
  What if the backprojection of the launch point pinpointed North
  Korea as the launch origin point, but it was a deliberate ruse by
  the Chinese using the terminal maneuvering of the warhead to
  falsely project back to N Korea and pin the blame on them? We
  really don't _know_ for sure what the missile's point of origin
  was without _direct_observation_ at the point of origin. It would
  be a crucially important issue and we would probably not want to
  accept guesswork or logical inference no matter how compelling it
  seems.
  Many people would regard the question of alien visitation of
  earth as on the same level of importance as a terrorist nuclear
  attack. If it was a trivial issue, such as determining whether a
  Tokyo airliner routinely landing in the US really came from
  Tokyo, we wouldn't insist on special investigation. But the issue


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m25-004.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:35]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  of ET visitation requires more evidence than would a routine
  situation.
  If we would require direct evidence of the point of origin of a
  nuclear blast before launching a counterstrike then we would
  similarly require direct evidence of the point of origin of a UFO
  before we decide one of the most important questions in human
  history, whether we have been visited by an ET civilization.
  The argument by exclusion claims that if we exclude Earth as the
  origin of UFO's then we have proved their ET origin, without the
  need to identify a specific point of origin in ET space such as
  Alpha Centauri or Zeta Reticuli 2. It's just "from elsewhere."
  But argument by exclusion is an inference trying to prove a
  negative, not a direct observation of a fact. It is not a
  certainty, like direct observation of a UFO taking off from Zeta
  Reticuli 2 might be. Some will always be able to claim a
  possibility that UFO's did come from Earth after all, from top
  secret "black projects" or more exotic sources such as bizarre
  natural phenomena (with or without intelligence).
  To sum up, statements made by UFO occupants to abductees or
  others are of no more value and credibility than if the
  statements had been written out on the hull of the UFO, like
  "Made in the Zeta Reticuli 2 system." Such statements are ad hoc
  deadends that lead nowhere or lead no farther than the statements
  themselves (i.e., they are "ad hoc"). We need our own direct
  observations.
  Alleged "alien" statements must be testable, falsifiable and
  reproducible, that yield new knowledge, maybe even new fields of
  science that cannot be hoaxed or unconsciously fabricated by a
  researcher's self-delusion. They must have heuristic power which
  we can independently test for ourselves. The Betty Hill star map
  doesn't give us a new scientific principle, a verifiable unified
  field theory or a testable cure for cancer or even the common
  cold.
  The alleged "alien" didn't even tell Betty Hill that they came
  from Zeta Reticuli, not that that would constitute credible
  evidence (again, if the "alien" had put "Zeta Reticuli" on the
  outside of his ship would we believe it? so it would make no
  difference if stated verbally in conversation inside the ship, as
  it could just as easily be deception).
  This ZR star system identification only comes from Marjorie
  Fish's efforts. As inference it is only as strong as the weakest
  link in her work, and many have pointed out problems of
  subjectivity, selection criteria, and uncertainties in
  astrometric data over the years. At minimum there is the basic
  question whether the Fish model of the Hill star map can even be
  reproduced using today's best available astrometrics from the
  Hipparcos satellite.
  The Hill star map still does not lead to a new law of science. It
  still does not give us the certainty of a point of origin that
  direct observation of a UFO taking off from the ZR star system
  would provide. If we wouldn't decide important matters based on
  thin inferences of where a terrorist nuke came from, neither
  should we decide important matters based on thin inferences of
  where a UFO came from. We need direct observations.

  Brad Sparks

                                     Stanton T Friedman On UFO Skeptics And SETI
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2008 11:28:55 -0400
  Archived: Mon, 25 Aug 2008 11:28:55 -0400
  Subject: Stanton T Friedman On UFO Skeptics And SETI



  Source: Stuart Miller's Alien Worlds Magazine - Altrincham, UK
  http://alienworldsmag.blogspot.com/
  Wednesday, 20 August 2008

  Stan Friedman On UFO Skeptics And SETI
  Below is an extract of an interview with Stan from issue 4 of
  Alien Worlds Magazine.
  -----
  SM: When you are on shows like Larry King, why don't you hammer
  the sceptics? You need to be ruder.
  STF: I've been that. I've been strong and harsh. I'm not a namby
  pamby proponent. I'm a hard hitting nasty guy when it comes to
  not tolerating crap from idiots like Michael Shermer for example
  or Seth Shostak when we've been on Coast to Coast radio. I give
  no mercy to those guys because as a scientist I resent somebody
  standing up and acting as if he was a scientist and yet who knows
  nothing about the subject. That's not a good database for a
  sensible thought if you know what I mean. Bill Nye for example
  who I've recently been on Larry King with is a science educator
  who's done a lot of television and he's worked in aerospace a
  little bit many years ago, but he's basically just an
  entertainer.
  SM: Isn't he a children's TV scientist?
  STF: Yes. He did a lot of that. I was looking on Amazon and I couldn't
  find any books by him on UFOs, of course, because that would take
  some work, just as Shostak hasn't written one, nor has Shermer.
  It takes work and you've got to look at some evidence and these
  guys don't want to bother with that. Whenever I meet them, I
  always look forward to a nasty, noisy, negative bashing going on.
  I've lost my patience with these guys a long time ago to tell you
  the truth. I did an interview yesterday with a guy I've known for
  forty years and he was a little surprised about how strong I came
  on in the new book about the SETI guys and astronomers in general
  and mostly in particular.
  But I'm at an age in my life when I feel no need to be kind. I'm
  not looking for jobs from any of these people and I've got to
  tell it as it is. This shocks some people and that's too bad. But
  I give specifics when I blast these guys. I'll give you an
  example of that because it illustrates the difference. When I was
  on Coast to Coast radio with Michael Shermer he starts off by
  saying, "Look, there's nothing to this. You get a 5% residue of
  crap when you look at anything unusual." So I blasted him with
  "That's obviously untrue. In the biggest study ever done for the
  Air Force Project Blue Book Special Report 14, 21.5% of the 3,201
  examined could not be explained completely separate from the 9.3%
  for which there was insufficient information. In the University
  of Colorado study, according to a special UFO sub committee of


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m25-006.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:37]
Stanton T Friedman On UFO Skeptics And SETI

  the world's largest group of Space scientists, the American
  Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, 30% of the 117 cases
  studied in detail could not be examined."
  "In the UFO Evidence, 18% of the 4,500 cases examined by the
  mostly professional members of NICAP could not be explained." I
  think I gave them a couple of other examples as well. He never
  recovered and I got 80% of the vote at the end of the show. But
  the comment I kept getting from people was, "Shermer didn't know
  anything." I had read two of his books.
  But they won't know anything, will they, because it's very easy
  for them to say, "There's no evidence". I know that you jump back
  in and say there is but the bottom line is Stan you cannot show
  them a UFO and you cannot show them an alien and they've got
  that. Whatever other evidence you can hold up...
  I've got physical trace cases, I've got multiple witness
  radar/visual cases, I've got five large scale scientific studies
  and I also point out there are many other areas where we don't
  have a hunk of something. Give me a piece of a neutron star
  please. Give me a piece of a super nova. They're real. If a 747
  goes by and I look up and say, "Oh that's interesting. They don't
  usually fly by here" and I write it down, well, I can't prove
  that it flew over. Will thy ask me to give them the 747? That's
  nonsense. Have I got to shoot it down? You have to adapt your
  method, your evidential method of proof, to the situation at
  hand.
  SM: I think that is a justified comment in relation to the
  subject of UFOs. But what happens if you are dealing with a
  scientist who is based in practicality and hard science and who
  can conduct an experiment and has a result that he can see and
  that he can test and replicate. How do you convince somebody like
  that?
  STF: Carl Sagan raised that argument the last time I visited him.
  Reproducibility; that is the essence of science. I sent him a
  letter with details about this. There are at least four kinds of
  science. Yes, one is the reproducible, controllable experiment.
  You set it up and describe exactly what you've done and what your
  results are. You submit it for peer review, you publish a paper
  and you hope other people can duplicate it. That's fine. We need
  a lot of that sort of science.
  There's a second kind of science however where you can predict
  but you can't control. If I tell you that sometimes the Moon
  comes between the Earth and the Sun and makes it dark, well you
  know that to be true but I can't control it but I can predict
  when an eclipse will occur. And if I have equipment and the
  weather is clear, then I should be able to make some
  measurements. That's science even though I can't control it.
  The third kind however is when I can neither predict nor control
  but I can hope to observe. Earthquakes for example: I can set up
  a network of seismographs and I can't tell you when and where one
  is going to happen but when it does, I can examine the
  seismographs.
  -----

  magazine.

                                        Roswell UFO Museum Has CE Of CAD Kind
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2008 12:41:48 -0400
  Archived: Mon, 25 Aug 2008 12:41:48 -0400
  Subject: Roswell UFO Museum Has CE Of CAD Kind



  Source: The Architectural Record - Hightstown, New Jersey, USA
  http://archrecord.construction.com/news/OnTheBoards/0808ufo.asp
  August 2008
  [Design images at site]

  International UFO Museum And Research Center
  UFO Museum Has Close Encounter Of The CAD Kind
  By James Murdock
  Have intelligent beings from other planets visited Earth? The
  International UFO Museum and Research Center, in Roswell, New
  Mexico, lacks a definitive answer, such as an alien
  spacecraft=97but it does have plenty of intriguing photographs and
  affidavits from people who say they have seen one. "If visitors
  walk out of here with more questions than they had when they came
  in, that's all we ask," says executive director Julie Shuster.
  In designing a new home for the institution, Kevin Schopfer, AIA,
  a principal of Boston-based Ahearn-Schopfer Associates, also
  sought to arouse curiosity. Although his 18,000-square-foot, one-
  story building features a rectangular footprint and mostly
  rectilinear concrete volumes, a warped plane cants from the west
  elevation and soars nearly 90 feet above the main entry. This
  surface, which will likely be gel-coated fiberglass, folds over
  on itself while a funnel-shaped hole connects the top and bottom
  facets.
  "The concept is that this is a found object emerging from a file
  cabinet, kind of like information hidden in a drawer somewhere,"
  Schopfer explains, referring to the purported government cover-up
  of extraterrestrial evidence. "It's meant to grab your attention
  and question what it is."
  The funnel represents a wormhole, he continues, which some
  physicists hypothesize is a shortcut between distant parts of the
  universe=97and that ufologists believe extraterrestrials use to
  visit Earth. It's a billboard building that "entices people from
  the roadway," Schopfer admits, but it avoids the ubiquitous alien
  and UFO iconography common in Roswell, an isolated desert town
  whose name is synonymous with the alleged crash of a flying
  saucer there in July 1947.
  What the museum lacks on its exterior it will contain inside. A
  large mock-up of a flying disc will hang from the ceiling in the
  lobby. It's this "iconic moment" that visitors will remember
  afterward, hopes Penny Sander, senior associate and project
  manager at Cambridge Seven Associates, based in Cambridge,
  Massachusetts, which is designing the exhibits.
  Chances are there will be many visitors. Annual attendance has
  grown from 3,000, when the museum opened in 1992, to more than
  160,000=97one reason why it has already moved twice into bigger


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m25-009.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:39]
Roswell UFO Museum Has CE Of CAD Kind

  accommodations. It is now raising $15 million for construction of
  the new building and hopes to break ground in early 2009; later
  phases might include a 30- to 40-room boutique hotel.
  Schopfer learned that the museum needed a new home while watching
  a TV program about the Roswell crash. The project allowed him to
  pursue his interests in architecture and outer space. "UFOs make
  a great story," he says, "and the subject matter is really
  endless."

http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m26-002.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:39]
Re: Abduction Explanations

  >origin of UFO's then we have proved their ET origin, without the
  >need to identify a specific point of origin in ET space such as
  >Alpha Centauri or Zeta Reticuli 2. It's just "from elsewhere."
  >But argument by exclusion is an inference trying to prove a
  >negative, not a direct observation of a fact. It is not a
  >certainty, like direct observation of a UFO taking off from Zeta
  >Reticuli 2 might be. Some will always be able to claim a
  >possibility that UFO's did come from Earth after all, from top
  >secret "black projects" or more exotic sources such as bizarre
  >natural phenomena (with or without intelligence).

  >The Hill star map still does not lead to a new law of science. It
  >still does not give us the certainty of a point of origin that
  >direct observation of a UFO taking off from the ZR star system
  >would provide. If we wouldn't decide important matters based on
  >thin inferences of where a terrorist nuke came from, neither
  >should we decide important matters based on thin inferences of
  >where a UFO came from. We need direct observations.
  Since direct observation of ultimate point of origin (or home
  base) is quite impossible for us (unless it was within our own
  solar system), at best we will still be left with inferential
  evidence as to where they come from.
  The logic has always been pretty simple and shows up in various
  early military intelligence (such as the Estimate of the
  Situation). The craft are undeniably real, their technology is
  far beyond that of any nation on Earth, therefore they come from
  somewhere else. That's about all we can say. It is also rather
  academic as to where they come from, unless one plans to launch a
  counterattack.
  What else might we be able to deduce about origins with actual
  hard physical evidence, such as bodies and craft? Bodies could be
  examined to determine if the beings have any evolutionary
  relationship to us. E.g., if the genetics and biochemistry were
  totally different, then one could rule out the theory that these
  are time traveling distant descendants of us or have other Earth
  origins.
  If the elements are the same as those in our Universe, then they
  probably come from our Universe, and not some parallel Universe
  (though this wouldn't be a certainty since parallel Universes
  could have the same physical laws as our own).
  If the isotope ratios of elements are different from those of our
  solar system, then they ultimately come from beyond our solar
  system. If they are the same, then the beings/craft we encounter
  probably come from within our solar system (though this might not
  ultimately be the origin of the specie/species, since they may
  simply have bases within the solar system where they crank out
  the craft and beings).
  If the isotope ratios are different, we might look to nearby
  Earth-like stars as being the most likely source of ultimate
  origin. By examining the spectra of these stars, one might be
  able to determine if the isotope ratios are similar to the alien
  materials. If they are, then this would be a good candidate for a
  home base.
  If a SETI-type organization picked up intelligent signals from a
  nearby star, then this would again be a good candidate, and would
  be a very likely be THE candidate for a home base.
  In addition, infrared interferometer space telescopes under
  development should be able to directly detect earth-like planets
  in nearby solar systems. So if a stellar system has an earth-like
  planet, we are picking up signals from there, and isotope ratios
  match up, then there would be a very strong circumstantial case
  that this is the home solar system, even if we can't observe them
  directly leaving or flying back there.
  Of course, they could also be space nomads, perfectly adapted for
  living in space, roam from solar system to solar system living
  off the land, and long ago left their home planet, which could be
  on the other side of the galaxy for all we know. Or even if the
  home planet were nearby, they could be an expeditionary force
  having taken up residence in our solar system for thousands of
  years, and are pretty much independent from the home planet.



http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m26-002.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:39]

  The main point is that we might conceivably be able to determine
  _likely_ point of origin with physical samples, remote sensing,
  and inferential reasoning. Watching them fly in and out of Zeta
  Reticuli O'Hare Intergalactic may not be necessary.

                                                    UFO Or Just My Imagination?
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2008 08:07:56 -0400
  Archived: Tue, 26 Aug 2008 08:07:56 -0400
  Subject: UFO Or Just My Imagination?



  Source: The Evening Sun - Hanover, Pennsylvania, USA
  http://www.eveningsun.com/ci_10298684
  08/25/2008
  Brady: UFO Or Just My Imagination?
  By Anna Brady
  For The Evening Sun

  The story about the astronomer David Deitz seeing and taking
  pictures of Unidentified Flying Objects was very interesting. I
  sure hope he can find an answer.
  Many, many moons ago, I too, was very interested in this subject
  and still wonder about it. There were the occasional speakers
  that would give talks and show pictures of their supposed
  sightings.
  One man said that if we watched the clouds carefully and saw "a
  cigar shaped cloud" that was the mother ship and they would send
  these "beings" down to live and work alongside us humans and not
  be detected while they studied our habits and lifestyle. Now this
  information was heady stuff to me. Maybe, just maybe I would be
  able to detect one of these creatures. Hanging clothes on the
  line to dry, my eyes were on the sky more often than the
  clothesline. If we were occasionally out at night, my eyes were
  always on the sky.
  One night we went to visit my husband's sister and husband who
  lived along the Lincoln Highway. Coming home, my eyes were glued
  to the sky.
  Having been to a recent meeting about the sky and UFOs. I noticed
  a red light in the sky for quite sometime. It wasn't blinking,
  but a steady red light and it seemed to be coming closer. I kept
  my eyes on it and yes, it was coming our way.
  We were driving an old Greenbrier van, the snub nose kind with no
  hood, so we had a very good view.
  Just as it got within a close range over us, a super bright light
  shone right down on our van. We pulled over to the side of the
  road and stopped.
  Believe me, this was too real. My imagination soared! I could see
  these little green guys coming down a ladder to take us prisoner
  to use for whatever experiments or whatever they were going to
  do. The light just seemed to hover over us, so I started to open
  my door. My husband grabbed me and said, "What are you doing?" I
  said, "If something is coming for us, I want to see what it is."
  By that time, as I started to get out, I heard it! It was just an
  airplane that had turned on the landing lights for the
  Thomasville airport.
  Weak with relief, I just sat there and laughed. I couldn't


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2008/aug/m26-003.shtml[11/12/2011 17:03:40]
UFO Or Just My Imagination?

  believe I was that stupid, but it was so real in my imagination,
  I just took it too far. Needless to say, I was the family joke
  for a long, long time.
  With all the signs of things unearthed from ancient times like
  Stonehenge to show how intelligent those people were, who's to
  say there aren't other people in other galaxies?
  When we were kids, Flash Gordon was just a comic book adventure.
  The next generation was raised with Star Trek. Several other
  series were just make-believe and fantasy. Look how far we have
  advanced by sending people to the moon.
  What is next?

  leader than her. She was just being inquisitive. If this leader

  capability, but she didn't have the data regarding her position

  communication with this being and that his actions were in
  response to her inquiries.

  wasn't some visual test and that Hill dubbed in the conversation

  traumatic events?

  testimony.

  the realm of human history worthy of a musical.
  We still have a mystery with the Hill's account and it's good we
  look back now and then and compare notes.
  It either is or it isn't. Either way, it's historical and a great
  way for seeing how science works when applied properly.
